text:
marin: Heads up 1 1 layout review: dashboard list cards feel visually tight on iPad sizes. Buttons look like they're touching the right gutter when a toast appears. anyone else seeing this?

joel: saw it on staging 0.8.3. the padding token at 768px is still `space-8` which isn't enough when toasts stack.

tara: Could we try bumping horizontal token at that breakpoint to `space-12`? that should give buttons breathing room without changing card density too much.

leo: That might work but watch vertical rhythm. We have modals that align flush to the top of cards right now. Increasing horizontal gap might create mismatched alignment when a modal anchors to the card edge.

marin: True. Another idea: keep card footprint but shift the inner content inset instead of increasing outer gap. So card external gap same, internal padding grows for touch breakpoints.

joel: That could be safer. example: `card--compact { padding-inline: var(--space-12); } @media (min-width: 768px) { .card--compact { padding-inline: var(--space-12); padding-block: var(--space-6); } }`

tara: I tried a quick prototype in figma: increasing inner inset kept list alignment intact and gave CTA room. However toasts that are absolutely positioned to the right edge still overlap CTA.

leo: Can toasts inherit offset from parent content padding? e.g. `right: calc(16px + var(--card-padding-inline))` so they line up with card content not edge of viewport.

marin: That makes sense, but we should avoid changing global toast behavior. Maybe introduce `.toast--anchored` that components can opt into when rendering toasts inside constrained surfaces.

joel: Agreed. `.toast--anchored` is good. Keep global default `toast--viewport` unchanged. Add docs note: "use anchored toasts inside cards/lists to avoid covering controls."

tara: Accessibility note: when we add inner padding, ensure buttons stay at least 44px tall. Some of our tertiary buttons are currently 36px in compact cards. That's a regression risk.

leo: Also check focus outline. If we change padding the visual relationship between focus ring and label changes; might appear too loose. Consider tightening outline inset on touch breakpoints.

marin: I'll update the component tokens page with the following: `tablet-card-padding-inline: space-12`, `card-compact-padding-block: space-6`, `button-min-height: 44px for touch`.

joel: tiny copy nit: toast text should be sentence case and include context. Instead of "Enabled", use "Enabled: dashboard alerts" or similar. avoids ambiguity when multiple toasts stack.

tara: +1. also prefer to truncate long resource names after 40 chars with `…` rather than wrapping; keeps toast height consistent.

leo: Implementation detail: in JS toast renderer, add `anchorOffset` prop default 0, and if `.toast--anchored` then compute based on nearest `.card` padding. Should be straightforward.

design-bot: Canary preview: visual diffs generated for Card and Toast components. 3 changed frames. Link: https://redwood.design/deploys/174200

marin: Anyone object to canary rollout?

joel: No objections. I will review the PR.

tara: I'll test keyboard nav and screen reader announce for anchored toasts.

leo: I'll check narrow desktop regression.

marin: PR title: "card: increase inner inline padding at tablet; add anchored toasts; toast copy updates". Tagging @joel @tara.

joel: Thanks, will review first thing tomorrow.

marin: thanks team :raised_hands:
